report.verdict: September 2026 confirms New Jersey's structural bifurcation: iGaming win rose 13.0% to $274.8m and for a second straight month out-earned the nine Atlantic City floors ($227.8m, -1.3%), while online sports GGR fell 18.8% on a 1.3% football hold and FanDuel's lead over DraftKings collapsed from $15m to $3.4m. Total gaming revenue still grew 2.8% to $579.6m (9M: $5.39bn, +5.1%) and the state banked $82.7m of gross revenue tax at the 19.75% online rate — a rate the Treasury has no incentive to lower.
summary: **Regulator and framework.** The New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement (DGE, within the Attorney General's office; AG Jennifer Davenport, Interim DGE Director Mary Jo Flaherty) licenses and reports the market under the Casino Control Act; iGaming (since Nov 2013) and sports wagering (since June 2018) are tethered to the nine Atlantic City casino licensees and two racetrack licensees (Meadowlands, Monmouth Park). September 2026 results were released on 19 Oct 2026.

**Headline: total gaming revenue $579.6m, +2.8% YoY** (vs $563.7m), the second-highest September on record; nine-month GGR $5.39bn, +5.1% vs $5.13bn. Note Intergame mis-reported the month as a 2.8% *decline*; the DGE release and five other sources confirm growth.

**iGaming is now the largest product: $274.8m (+13.0%), 47.4% of total GGR**, nearly matching July's all-time record of $276.9m and the third-highest month ever. 9M iGaming win $2.40bn (+13.2% vs $2.12bn). Online casino has out-earned the physical casino floor two months running.

**Growth is decelerating but still double-digit:** iGaming grew >24% in 2024 and 21.8% in 2025 (WSN); 2026 YTD +13.2% with August at only +4.4% before September rebounded to +13.0%. Incumbents FanDuel (+2.1%) and DraftKings (+9.9%) are growing slower than the market; share is being bought by Fanatics (+187%), Hard Rock Bet (+25.5%), BetRivers (+25.2%) and bet365 (+52.8%).

**Sports betting is the weak leg: GGR $77.0m (-14.3%)**, online $72.9m (-18.8%), retail lounges $4.1m (vs a $13k loss a year ago). Completed-event handle fell 3.6% to $1.09bn with one fewer NFL Sunday; hold compressed to 6.3% from 7.3%. Football produced just $4.3m on $318.8m of handle (1.3% hold vs 4.8%). 9M GGR $748.4m (-6.3%); handle $8.30bn (-4.1%) and down in seven of nine months (June/July World Cup the exceptions).

**Operator landscape — online duopoly eroding.** On DGE's YTD-August combined iGaming+OSB classification FanDuel held 26.7% share, DraftKings 19.5%, BetMGM 11.7%, Borgata 6.4%, Caesars 6.0%, Fanatics 5.8%, Hard Rock Bet 5.6%, BetRivers 3.3%, Golden Nugget 2.9%, bet365 2.8%. In September online sports, FanDuel ($24.7m, -34.4%) and DraftKings ($21.3m, -5.9%) still took 63.1% of online GGR but the gap shrank to $3.4m from $15m; bet365 is now #3 ($6.6m, +21.2%).

**Land-based Atlantic City: $227.8m (-1.3%)**; slots +4.6% to $177.9m but tables -17.6% to $49.9m (Borgata tables -48.1% to $9.0m), with a rare nor'easter over the 25 Sept weekend. Borgata $55.7m (-11.3%) leads; Hard Rock $43.4m (-4.3%); Ocean $42.6m (+7.6%) is now within $0.8m of Hard Rock; Harrah's +12.7% to $18.5m. 9M casino win $2.24bn (+1.4%) but only three of nine properties are up YTD.

**Tax regime — GGR base, online at 19.75%.** DGE tax statistics (Aug-26 PDF) show: casino 8% gross revenue tax + 1.25% Investment Alternative Tax (IAT); internet gaming 19.75% GRT + 2.5% IAT; online sports (casino and racetrack) 19.75% GRT + 1.25% additional tax; retail sportsbook lounges 8.5% + 1.25%. The online rates were lifted from 15% (iGaming) and 13% (OSB) with effect from 1 Jul 2025 under the FY2026 budget [rate change date not re-verified this session]; 2026 is the first full calendar year at 19.75%.

**Tax take: $82.7m gross revenue taxes in September; $756.8m 9M.** The DGE headline excludes IATs and the 1.25% add-ons; all-in gaming taxes were $92.4m in August vs the $81.5m headline, so September all-in is ~$93m (est.). Blended effective GRT is ~14.3% of GGR. Recipients (Aug): Casino Revenue Fund $76.6m, Atlantic City PILOT (IATs) $10.2m, State General Fund (racetrack OSB) $4.8m, CRDA marketing $0.46m, racetrack municipalities $0.32m.

**Licensing regime.** Market access requires a contract with one of 9 casino licensees or 2 racetracks; DGE classifies brands as third-party (66.0% of online GGR YTD-Aug), joint venture (BetMGM/Borgata, 18.8%), affiliate (Caesars, Hard Rock Bet; 12.8%) or casino-own (2.4%). DGE's August report lists 28 active iGaming brands and 15 active online sportsbook entries (14 distinct brands). Statutory fees — internet gaming permit $400k initial / $250k annual renewal; sports wagering licence $100k initial; up to 3 OSB skins per licensee — are from prior knowledge and are [unverified] in this session.

**Online penetration is 60.0% of GGR** (iGaming + online sports = $347.7m of $579.6m), up from 59.1% a year ago; 9M online share 58.1%. Retail sports is immaterial (5.3% of sports GGR) and the land-based floor is a slowly shrinking 39% of the market.

**Poker is structurally in decline:** peer-to-peer win was $2.56m in August (-3.2%) and $20.1m YTD-Aug (-2.8%); PartyPoker fell 47.5% to $0.92m in September and PokerStars exited the state in 2026 (nil revenue from August).

**Payments reality:** New Jersey allows the full US online funding stack (ACH/e-check, debit, PayPal, Play+, cash at cage/PayNearMe) and — unlike several newer states — credit-card deposits remain permitted; bills to prohibit credit-card funding have been introduced but not enacted as far as we could verify [unverified this session].

**Responsible gambling and advertising:** DGE operates statewide online/casino self-exclusion and since 2023 requires operators to run analytics-based at-risk player identification; Gaming Intelligence reported on 20-21 Oct 2026 that DGE has further 'strengthened' online RG requirements — we could not read the detail and flag it as a live compliance item. There is no statutory advertising ban; promotion is governed by DGE advertising regulations/guidance.

**Enforcement and political direction.** DGE has been assertive on unlicensed verticals — cease-and-desist action against sports-event prediction markets (Kalshi/Robinhood, 2025, litigation ongoing at the time of our last verified data) and legislative action against sweepstakes casinos [status unverified]. Fiscal direction is clear: the state has already raised online rates once and the 19.75% level is below neighbouring Pennsylvania (36% OSB) and New York (51%), leaving headroom for further increases.

**Benchmarking:** in September New Jersey sportsbooks kept $77.0m vs Pennsylvania's $44.7m and Massachusetts' ~$75m, yet Pennsylvania collected more sports tax ($16.1m vs ~$14.4m implied for NJ online at 19.75%) — illustrating that NJ's attraction is volume and product breadth, not low tax.

**Read-through for B2Tech:** New Jersey is the deepest, most liquid and most mature US online casino market (annualising ~$3.3bn iGaming win) with a stable GGR-based tax and open skin access, but it is late-cycle: 28 iGaming brands compete for ~61% top-4 concentration, new entrants are growing only via heavy promotion (WSN), online sports is contracting, and the iGaming statutory authorisation runs to November 2028 [unverified] — entry economics hinge on a cost-efficient market-access deal and casino-led differentiation rather than sportsbook.

segments.name: Online casino (Internet gaming)
segments.headline: $274.8m (+13.0%) — now the state's largest product and bigger than the Atlantic City floor; growth slowing, share shifting to challengers.
narrative: Internet gaming win of $274.8m in September 2026 was up 13.0% on $243.1m a year earlier, the third-highest month on record and within $2m of July's $276.9m peak. Nine-month win reached $2.40bn (+13.2% vs $2.12bn), implying a 2026 full-year outcome of roughly $3.25–3.3bn (est.). The product now generates 47.4% of all New Jersey gaming revenue (43.1% a year ago) and for the second consecutive month exceeded the combined win of the nine land-based casinos by ~$47m. The tax base is 'Internet Gaming Gross Revenue' (win less DGE-approved adjustments, including a limited deduction for promotional gaming credits), taxed at 19.75% plus a 2.5% Investment Alternative Tax that funds the Atlantic City PILOT.

The brand table shows a market whose leaders are maturing while the second tier buys share. FanDuel (Golden Nugget licence) stayed #1 at $57.8m but grew just 2.1%; DraftKings (Resorts) was $53.3m (+9.9%), narrowing the gap to $4.5m from $8.2m; BetMGM (Borgata joint venture) $35.4m (+16.7%); Borgata's own brand $22.0m (+6.0%); Caesars Palace (CIENJ) $20.2m (+8.4%). These five hold ~68% of the market and the top four 61.3%. Below them the growth is striking: Hard Rock Bet $17.8m (+25.5%, 9M $159.6m +40.7%), Fanatics (Bally's licence) $14.7m (+187.4% from $5.1m), Golden Nugget $11.0m (+17.5%), BetRivers $10.0m (+25.2%) and bet365 (Hard Rock licence) $4.0m (+52.8%). WSN's read — which we share — is that much of the incremental growth is promotion-funded by a handful of entrants, so reported win overstates the margin pool.

Year-to-date the picture is similar: FanDuel $541.1m (+14.5%), DraftKings $423m (+0.8%), BetMGM $307.1m (+11.6%). DraftKings' flat YTD performance against a +13% market is the most notable share loss among incumbents. Poker continues to shrink — peer-to-peer win was $2.56m in August (-3.2%) and $20.1m for 8M (-2.8%); PartyPoker fell 47.5% to $0.9m in September and PokerStars reported nil from August after exiting; Tropicana's own brand fell 45.2% to $1.6m and Jackpocket 36.1% to $0.7m. Over 30 brands have been live in the past year but DGE's August list shows 28 active, with the long tail (Playstar, Mohegan Sun, Monopoly, WSOP, Wheel of Fortune, Betinia, Ember, Vegas Club, Resorts World) each below 1% share.

Commercially, this is the most liquid online casino market in the US and the clearest proof-point that iGaming can grow double-digits a decade after launch. But for a new entrant the maths are unforgiving: at 19.75% + 2.5% tax, a market-access fee to a casino licensee, and promotional intensity that is visibly rising, the realistic path is a differentiated casino product under an affiliate or third-party skin, not a me-too sportsbook-led bundle. The classification data (third-party brands 66.0% of online GGR YTD-Aug; joint venture 18.8%; affiliate 12.8%; casino-own 2.4%) confirms that licensees monetise access rather than operate — which keeps skins available but prices them.

segments.name: Sports betting (online + retail)
segments.headline: GGR $77.0m (-14.3%) on a 1.3% football hold and one fewer NFL Sunday; online -18.8%, duopoly share slipping to bet365/DraftKings.
narrative: Sports wagering gross revenue was $77.0m in September 2026, down 14.3% from $89.8m. Online sportsbooks produced $72.9m (-18.8%), 94.7% of the total, while the retail lounges swung to $4.1m from a $13k loss. Completed-event handle fell 3.6% to $1.09bn (from $1.13bn) and statewide hold on completed events compressed to 6.3% from 7.3%. The culprit was football: handle fell 15.3% to $318.8m (one fewer NFL Sunday than September 2025) and operator win collapsed 76.4% to $4.3m — a 1.3% hold versus 4.8% — as favourites and popular parlay legs landed. Parlays remained the largest category at $380.6m of handle (+0.6%) but win fell 10.5% to $45.0m as parlay hold slipped to 11.8% from 13.3%; baseball was comparatively strong.

The year-to-date trend is negative in volume, not just luck: 9M GGR $748.4m (-6.3% vs $798.5m), online $730.8m (-6.4%), retail $17.5m (flat), handle $8.30bn (-4.1%) and down in seven of nine months. Only June and July grew, lifted by the FIFA World Cup (June handle $917.2m, +16%, though hold was just 6.24% and GGR fell 37.7%; July GGR rebounded to $97m with online +25.5%). August's -25% was blamed by DGE on a later start to the college-football calendar. Our reading is that New Jersey has passed peak handle: New York's launch in 2022 removed the cross-border commuter base, prediction-market and offshore leakage is non-trivial, and the market is now a hold-driven revenue story.

Brand dynamics are the most important development. FanDuel (Meadowlands) fell 34.4% to $24.7m while DraftKings (Resorts) fell only 5.9% to $21.3m; their combined share of online GGR is 63.1% but the gap shrank to $3.4m from $15m. bet365 (Hard Rock) is now a clear #3 at $6.6m (+21.2%; YTD +35.7%), ahead of BetMGM $6.3m (-10.7%; YTD +6.9%) and Fanatics $4.9m (-29.2%; YTD +8.2%). Caesars generated $3.2m across its two licences (-12.1%), Hard Rock Bet $2.3m (+36%), theScore Bet $1.7m (-31.5%). On DGE's YTD-August full-year ranking, FanDuel had $262.1m (-6.7%), DraftKings $173.9m (-13.0%), Fanatics $56.2m (+13.4%), BetMGM $54.5m (+9.4%), bet365 $51.8m (+37.8%) — three mid-tier brands growing double-digits while the two leaders shrink.

Fiscally, online sports is taxed at 19.75% of GGR plus a 1.25% additional tax (casino-licensed books → CRDA marketing; racetrack books → host municipalities); lounge revenue at 8.5% + 1.25%. Racetrack online tax flows to the State General Fund ($4.7m in August), casino-partner online tax to the Casino Revenue Fund. Implied September online sports tax is ~$14.4m, below Pennsylvania's $16.1m collected on far lower GGR ($44.7m) because of PA's 36% rate — a comparison the New Jersey Treasury will not have missed. For an operator the product is mature, promotion-heavy and structurally #3-and-below; the only growth evidence is for brands with a differentiated proposition (bet365's pricing/in-play depth, Fanatics' loyalty ecosystem).

segments.name: Atlantic City land-based casinos
segments.headline: Casino win $227.8m (-1.3%): slots +4.6%, tables -17.6% (Borgata -48%), nor'easter weekend; only three of nine properties up YTD.
narrative: The nine Atlantic City casino hotels won $227.8m in September, down 1.3% from $230.7m, with a rare nor'easter over the 25–26 September weekend and unfavourable table-game outcomes. Slot win rose 4.6% to $177.9m but table win fell 17.6% to $49.9m from $60.6m, with five properties reporting table declines. Borgata alone explains the citywide shortfall: its table win halved (-48.1% to $9.0m) while slots grew 2.9% to $46.7m, leaving total win of $55.7m (-11.3%), a ~$7.1m decline against a +$4.1m aggregate gain at the other eight properties. Nine-month casino win was $2.24bn (+1.4%), a $31.8m gain, but only three properties are ahead of 2025 YTD — Borgata ($612.4m, +2.1%), Ocean ($372.5m, +5.6%) and Caesars (+10.9% through August).

Property dynamics are tightening at the top. Hard Rock won $43.4m (-4.3%) and Ocean $42.6m (+7.6%), narrowing the gap to $0.8m from $5.8m; Ocean led the city in table win at $14.8m. Harrah's posted the strongest percentage gain (+12.7% to $18.5m, tables +43.5%). Through August the laggards were Bally's (-2.3% YTD, $89.6m), Golden Nugget (-4.7%, $90.0m), Resorts (-2.3%, $107.0m) and Tropicana (-2.6%, $149.1m) — the four smallest floors, each sub-$150m YTD, which is where consolidation or licence-transfer risk sits.

Land-based gaming is taxed at 8% of gross revenue (with a promotional-gaming-credit adjustment) plus a 1.25% IAT distributed under the Atlantic City PILOT statute; August casino taxes were $21.9m ($18.3m GRT + $3.7m IAT). The retail floor has become the market's low-growth, high-cost segment — the Casino Association has repeatedly cited record operating costs — and its strategic value to an online entrant is as a licence host, not a revenue line. All nine licensees now sponsor online skins, and licence-holder online revenue (Golden Nugget hosting FanDuel/BetRivers, Resorts hosting DraftKings, Borgata/BetMGM, CIENJ hosting Caesars/BetParx/Jackpocket, Hard Rock hosting bet365, Bally's hosting Fanatics) is now a material share of property-level economics.

segments.name: Licensing & tax regime
segments.headline: GGR-based tax, 19.75% online since July 2025; access tethered to 9 casinos + 2 racetracks; iGaming authorisation runs to Nov 2028 [unverified].
narrative: New Jersey taxes gross gaming revenue, not turnover, and splits the take by channel. Per the DGE's August 2026 gaming-tax statistics: casinos pay an 8% gross revenue tax plus a 1.25% Investment Alternative Tax; internet gaming pays 19.75% plus a 2.5% IAT; online sports wagering pays 19.75% (both casino-partnered and racetrack-partnered books) plus a 1.25% additional tax; retail sportsbook lounges pay 8.5% plus 1.25%. The 19.75% online rates replaced 15% (iGaming) and 13% (online sports) from 1 July 2025 under the FY2026 Appropriations Act — the first rate increase since launch — after Governor Murphy had originally proposed 25% [the increase and its effective date are from prior knowledge and were not re-verified in this session]. Gaming taxes are unaudited and subject to adjustment; the casino GRT line embeds the tax effect of promotional gaming credits, and internet gaming returns deduct promotional credits above a threshold.

Headline tax take was $82.7m for September and $756.8m for the nine months. The DGE press-release figure is gross revenue tax only; adding IATs and the 1.25% add-ons, August's all-in gaming taxes were $92.4m (headline $81.5m) and $760.9m for eight months, so all-in 2026 collections are tracking ~$1.15bn (est.). The money is earmarked: Casino Revenue Fund (casino, iGaming and casino-partner sports GRT: $76.6m in August; funds senior/disabled programmes), Atlantic City PILOT (IATs: $10.2m), State General Fund (racetrack sports GRT: $4.8m), CRDA marketing ($0.46m) and racetrack municipalities ($0.32m). This earmarking is politically protective of the industry but also makes the Treasury highly sensitive to online growth — iGaming alone contributed $57.7m of August's $92.4m.

Licensing is tethered. iGaming requires an internet gaming permit held by an Atlantic City casino licensee, with brands operating as skins under a market-access agreement; sports wagering licences are held by the nine casinos and two racetracks (Meadowlands — FanDuel's host — and Monmouth Park), each permitted a limited number of online skins (statutory cap of three per licensee [unverified]). DGE's classification of online revenue (third-party 66.0%, joint-venture 18.8%, affiliate 12.8%, casino-own 2.4% YTD-Aug) shows the economic model is rental of access. Statutory fees we believe apply — internet gaming permit $400,000 initial and $250,000 annual renewal, sports wagering licence $100,000 initial, plus a $250,000 annual responsible-gambling contribution per internet permit — are [unverified] in this session and should be confirmed against N.J.S.A. 5:12 and N.J.A.C. 13:69O before modelling. Every platform, vendor and key employee requires DGE licensing (casino service industry enterprise licence or vendor registration), and iGaming servers must sit in approved New Jersey facilities.

Two legal clocks matter. First, the internet-gaming authorisation is time-limited: the 2023 extension pushed sunset to November 2028 [unverified], so a renewal bill — and the leverage it gives the Legislature to revisit the rate — is due in the 2027–28 session. Second, the 2025 tax rise closed the gap to neighbours only partially (Pennsylvania 54% slots-equivalent online / 36% OSB; New York 51% OSB) and the next budget cycle (FY2028, Feb–Jun 2027) under Governor Sherrill is the obvious venue for another look. Our base case is that 19.75% holds through 2027, with a non-trivial risk of a move toward 25% tied to the 2028 reauthorisation.

segments.name: Payments, responsible gambling, advertising & enforcement
segments.headline: Open funding stack incl. credit cards; DGE tightening online RG (Oct 2026); enforcement focus on prediction markets and sweepstakes; political direction is fiscal, not prohibitionist.
narrative: Payments are not a constraint in New Jersey. Operators accept ACH/e-check, debit cards, PayPal and similar wallets, prepaid Play+ cards, PayNearMe and cash at the partner casino cage; credit-card deposits remain permitted, which distinguishes New Jersey from several newer US states and from the UK. Legislative proposals to ban credit-card funding and to cap deposits have been introduced in recent sessions but, to our knowledge, none has been enacted [unverified this session]. Geolocation and KYC are mandated at account level, with servers and player-account systems subject to DGE technical standards and independent lab certification.

Responsible-gambling obligations are among the most prescriptive in the US and are tightening. DGE runs the statewide self-exclusion programme (online and casino; one-year, five-year and lifetime options) and, since its 2023 Responsible Gaming Best Practices, requires operators to deploy analytics that identify at-risk play and to intervene; operator-funded contributions support the Council on Compulsive Gambling of NJ. On 20–21 October 2026 Gaming Intelligence reported that New Jersey has further 'enhanced' online responsible-gaming requirements — we could not read the detail within this session, but it should be treated as a near-term compliance cost item (likely in the areas of limit-setting, affordability-style monitoring and marketing to at-risk cohorts). Advertising is governed by DGE regulation and guidance rather than a statutory ban; there is no watershed, but inducement advertising must be truthful, carry 1-800-GAMBLER messaging and avoid targeting minors or self-excluded players, and the Legislature has periodically considered restrictions on college-campus partnerships and 'risk-free' language.

Enforcement has become the DGE's defining posture. In 2025 it issued cease-and-desist orders to Kalshi and Robinhood over sports-event contracts, triggering federal litigation over CFTC pre-emption that was still unresolved at the limit of our verified data; the outcome will determine whether a tax-free, licence-free substitute for sportsbooks can operate in the state. The Legislature has also moved against sweepstakes-model casinos [enactment status unverified], and DGE continues to publicise actions against unlicensed offshore sites. Direction of travel is therefore protective of the licensed, taxed channel — the state wants the ~$1.15bn of annual gaming taxes defended, not the activity suppressed. The leadership backdrop — Interim Director Mary Jo Flaherty since 2024, a new Attorney General and a new Governor (Sherrill, from January 2026) — means the first permanent DGE Director appointment of the new administration and the FY2028 budget are the two events to watch for any change in tone.

highlights.text: Deepest online casino market in the US: iGaming win $274.8m in September (+13.0%), $2.40bn for 9M (+13.2%), annualising ~$3.3bn — and still growing double-digits 13 years after launch, with online now 60% of state GGR.

Share is demonstrably contestable: Fanatics (+187% to $14.7m), Hard Rock Bet (+25.5%), BetRivers (+25.2%) and bet365 (+52.8% casino, +21.2% sports) are taking share from FanDuel/DraftKings, whose online sports gap shrank from $15m to $3.4m — challengers can scale here.

GGR-based tax with a stable, earmarked take ($82.7m headline in September; ~$93m all-in est.): no turnover tax, promotional-credit adjustments allowed, and the Casino Revenue Fund earmark gives the industry a political constituency.

Open skin/market-access model: 28 active iGaming brands and 14 online sportsbook brands ride on 9 casino + 2 racetrack licences; third-party brands already generate 66% of online GGR, so licensees are willing hosts.

Payments and product breadth are unconstrained: credit cards, wallets and cash all permitted; slots, tables, live dealer and poker all legal; no statutory ad ban — a full-stack proposition can be deployed without the product carve-outs seen in other US states.
Regulator enforcement protects the licensed channel: DGE action against prediction markets and the legislative move against sweepstakes reduce grey-market competition for taxed operators.
Retail sports lounges swung to +$4.1m and World Cup months (June/July) showed handle can still grow +16% on event catalysts — 2026 FIFA World Cup legacy and 2027 NFL calendar offer timing upside.

lowlights.text: Online sports betting is contracting: 9M GGR -6.3%, handle -4.1% and down in seven of nine months; September online GGR -18.8% with football hold at 1.3% — a structurally lower-hold, lower-volume market since New York's launch.

Tax ratchet risk: online rates already rose from 15%/13% to 19.75% in July 2025 [date unverified]; neighbours tax at 36–51% and the Nov 2028 iGaming reauthorisation [unverified] gives the Legislature leverage to revisit the rate in the FY2028 budget.

Growth is promotion-funded and slowing: iGaming growth has decelerated from >24% (2024) and 21.8% (2025) to 13.2% YTD with August at +4.4%; challengers' gains come with heavy marketing, and DraftKings is flat YTD — margin pool is tighter than reported win suggests.

Concentration and access cost: top-4 iGaming brands hold 61.3%, FanDuel+DraftKings 63% of online sports; every entrant must pay a market-access fee to a casino licensee on top of 22.25% all-in iGaming tax, compressing contribution margins for a sub-3% share player.
Compliance cost is rising: DGE enhanced online RG requirements in October 2026 (detail not read) on top of mandatory at-risk analytics; credit-card deposit and advertising bills recur each session.

Prediction-market pre-emption litigation (Kalshi/Robinhood v. DGE) is unresolved at our data limit; an adverse federal ruling would legitimise an untaxed, unlicensed sports substitute inside the state.
Land-based floor is ex-growth (9M +1.4%; only 3 of 9 properties up) with the four smallest casinos sub-$150m YTD — licence-host instability or consolidation could disrupt skin agreements.

forecast.intro: The regulatory bridge from 2025 to 2026 is already in the numbers: the July 2025 lift of online rates to 19.75% (from 15% iGaming / 13% OSB) means 2026 is the first full calendar year at the new rate, and the DGE's 9M headline gross-revenue-tax take of $756.8m (all-in ~$854m est. including IATs) is running ~15–20% ahead of the revenue growth it sits on. On our extrapolation of DGE data, 2026 total gaming revenue lands at ~$7.2bn (est., +4–5%), driven entirely by iGaming (~$3.25–3.3bn, +12–13%) offsetting sports GGR of ~$1.0bn (-5–7%) and a flat Atlantic City floor (~$2.9bn). All-in 2026 gaming taxes should approach ~$1.15bn (est.), of which iGaming contributes well over half — which is precisely why the next rule changes will be fiscal (rate, reauthorisation terms, promo-deduction limits) rather than structural.

forecast.view: **Market:** we expect iGaming growth to settle at **8–12% in 2027** as the law of large numbers and promotional fatigue bite, with FanDuel/DraftKings share drifting below 40% combined of online casino and the Fanatics/Hard Rock/bet365 tier reaching ~20%; online casino will exceed 50% of state GGR during 2027. Sports GGR is **flat-to-down structurally** (handle ex-events declining 3–5% p.a.), with revenue volatility dominated by NFL hold; any recovery depends on parlay mix and the outcome of the prediction-market litigation. The land-based floor stays within ±2%. **Rules:** base case is the 19.75% online rate holds through FY2027, but we assign a **meaningful probability (~35–40%) of a rate increase toward 22.5–25% being attached to the iGaming reauthorisation needed before November 2028**, alongside tighter promo-credit deductibility; RG rules will tighten incrementally (October 2026 changes are the start, affordability-style monitoring is the direction); advertising restrictions will stay guidance-led rather than statutory. **Leverage for an entrant** lies in a long-dated market-access agreement signed before reauthorisation, casino-led product differentiation, and a sportsbook kept as a retention tool rather than an acquisition engine.
watch: DGE October 2026 enhanced online responsible-gaming requirements — read the rule text and compliance deadline (reported by Gaming Intelligence 20–21 Oct 2026, not read in this session).
FY2028 budget cycle (Governor's address Feb/Mar 2027; enactment by 30 Jun 2027) — any proposal to move online rates above 19.75% or to limit promotional-credit deductions.
iGaming reauthorisation bill ahead of the November 2028 sunset [date unverified] — watch for conditions (rate, RG, server, skin caps) attached to renewal.
Outcome of DGE v. Kalshi/Robinhood prediction-market litigation (Third Circuit / Supreme Court) — determines whether untaxed sports-event contracts are lawful in New Jersey.
Appointment of a permanent DGE Director under Governor Sherrill — first signal of enforcement and licensing tone.
Monthly DGE releases: watch whether iGaming growth stays >10% into Q4 (October release ~mid-Nov 2026) and whether NFL hold normalises toward 7–8%.
New York iGaming legalisation — the single largest demand-side threat to NJ iGaming (cross-border players) and the biggest swing factor for 2027–28 growth.
Atlantic City property M&A / licence transfers among the four sub-$150m floors — risk to existing market-access agreements and opportunity to secure a host.
